entries.subject: Sierra tag push: use documented PUT /leads/{id} {tags:[tag]} / {removeTags:[tag]}
entries.title: Sierra tag push: use documented PUT /leads/{id} {tags:[tag]} / {removeTags:[tag]}
entries.body:

and `removeTags` removes — so sending only the single changed tag never touches
existing tags. Confirmed working: a test push added FSBO_Off Market while keeping
the lead's other tags. Object form 400s; strings are required. Earlier "clobber"
was a transient empty read right after the write (Sierra eventual consistency).

entries.subject: Stability: stop crashing on stray errors (IMAP socket + resilient handler + crash log)
entries.title: Stability: stop crashing on stray errors (IMAP socket + resilient handler + crash log)
entries.body:
Root cause of the recurring "Exited with status 1" emails: the Gmail IMAP client
(polled every 60s) had no 'error' listener, so a dropped socket emitted an
unhandled 'error' event that crashed the whole process. Node treats an unhandled
EventEmitter 'error' as fatal.

- gmail-inbox.js: add client.on('error', ...) so a dropped IMAP socket is absorbed.
- index.js: uncaughtException now LOGS + keeps the Hub running instead of exit(1).
  A single background/socket error no longer takes the service down or pages the
  team. State is disk-backed (better-sqlite3 transactions), so surviving is safe.
- Crashes are recorded to /data/crash-log.jsonl and readable at GET /api/crash-log,
  so the next incident leaves a stack trace we can actually diagnose.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: DB engine: migrate sql.js (WASM, whole-DB-in-RAM) to better-sqlite3 (native, reads/writes file directly)
entries.title: DB engine: migrate sql.js (WASM, whole-DB-in-RAM) to better-sqlite3 (native, reads/writes file directly)
entries.body:
Root-cause fix for the 512MB OOM crashes: the old sql.js layer held the entire
66MB DB in RAM and serialized a fresh copy on every save. better-sqlite3 reads and
writes the SQLite file on disk directly, so steady-state memory is a small fraction.

- import better-sqlite3; openDbFile() sets journal_mode=DELETE (file-copy backups
  stay valid), synchronous=FULL (durable), foreign_keys=OFF (matches prior behavior)
- makeDbShim() keeps the exact sql.js-compatible surface (run/get/all/exec/prepare/
  export/pragma/close) so ~200 call sites + schema DDL are unchanged
- sanitizeParams(): undefined -> NULL, boolean -> 0/1 (better-sqlite3 rejects both)
- beginBulk/endBulk are now real BEGIN/COMMIT transactions (depth-counted, ROLLBACK
  on failure); saveDb() is a NO-OP (writes already hit disk). This removes the
  serialize-on-save path that caused the 2026-05-20 corruption.
- boot: quick_check on load; candidate/restore validate with a readonly quick_check
- migration column reads use db.all("PRAGMA table_info(x)").map(r=>r.name) and
  integrity check uses db.pragma('integrity_check',{simple:true})

Verified locally end-to-end: insert/get/all, undefined->NULL, boolean->int, bulk
transactions, update, settings round-trip, health, on-disk persistence (a separate
connection sees writes immediately), integrity ok.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.title: Sierra-sync slowdown: atomic saveDb + bulk-mode batching
entries.body:

the live DB — a crash mid-write can no longer truncate/corrupt the file
(this was the missing safeguard behind the 2026-05-20 corruption).

loop in beginBulk()/endBulk() so every lead flushes as ONE atomic save
instead of a full ~40 MB write per lead. Eliminates the 14-23s event-loop

guarantees bulk mode always exits even on sync error.

Verified on a copy of real data: 1743 existing rows preserved, 250 bulk

entries.subject: Auto-restore: tighten data-preservation guarantee
entries.title: Auto-restore: tighten data-preservation guarantee
entries.body:
Two changes per user request "make sure 100% no existing data removed":

1. Copy corrupt file to sidecar FIRST, then overwrite live file. Was
   rename-then-copy, which left a brief window where the corrupt bytes
   only existed in the renamed sidecar - if anything went wrong after
   the rename but before the backup copy completed, the live position
   would be missing.

2. If the sidecar copy fails (disk full, permission, etc.), ABORT the
   entire restore. Crash with the original corruption error and leave
   the live file untouched. Previous code would still try to overwrite
   the live file with the backup even if it couldn't preserve the
   corrupt bytes - that's a hidden data-loss path.

Net safety: regardless of failure mode, the original corrupted bytes
are either at DB_PATH (if abort) or at DB_PATH.corrupt-{ts} (if
restore succeeded). They are never deleted, never overwritten without
a copy existing elsewhere first.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Auto-restore from newest valid backup when live DB is corrupted
entries.title: Auto-restore from newest valid backup when live DB is corrupted
entries.body:
Today's incident: the bulk-mode commit (4450c8c) corrupted
/data/realestate-hub.db ("database disk image is malformed"). Server
correctly refused to boot (per the no-auto-rename policy that prevents
silent data wipes), so deploys went into a crash loop and the service
sat at 502.

Added a recovery branch: when sql.js fails to load the DB, walk every
sidecar file in /data/ and every file in /data/backups/, validate each
by attempting to load it with sql.js + PRAGMA quick_check, and swap in
the newest one that loads cleanly.

Safety properties:
- Corrupt file is renamed to .corrupt-{timestamp} (never deleted)
- Skips the pre-boot snapshot taken on THIS boot if it matches the
  corrupt file's size+mtime (it's a copy of the corrupt file)
- Falls back to the original crash if NO valid candidate exists
- Logs are loud so the user sees exactly which file was restored

The recovery window equals the time since the most recent valid backup
(typically <24h with the daily 2 AM backup). That's an acceptable cost
vs. the current state of "service down indefinitely until a human
shells into Render and swaps files manually".

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Sierra incremental sync: wrap in bulk mode to stop blocking API requests
entries.title: Sierra incremental sync: wrap in bulk mode to stop blocking API requests
entries.body:
processLead() does INSERTs/UPDATEs, and db.run() saves the entire sql.js
DB to disk after each write when not in bulk mode. For a 45K-lead DB
that's multi-hundred-ms of synchronous blocking per lead. The recently
added second pass (creationDate) compounds it. Net result: every 10 min
the event loop is starved for 10-30 seconds, and any other API request
(Partners list, Vendors list, etc.) queues behind it.

Wrapped both passes + the sync_log insert in beginBulk/endBulk so we
serialize the DB to disk ONCE at the end of the sync instead of per
lead. try/finally guarantees endBulk runs even if Sierra throws.

Concrete symptom this fixes: user reported Vendors/Partners taking
20+ seconds to load. Probed /api/partners with no-auth and got
401 in 21.7s -- the auth middleware was waiting for the event loop
to be free.

entries.subject: HOTFIX: checkDbHealth crashes with 'db.get is not a function'
entries.title: HOTFIX: checkDbHealth crashes with 'db.get is not a function'
entries.body:

sql.js Database instance - that object has .exec() and .prepare() but
NO .get() method. The wrapper get() function (which uses .prepare/.step
internally) is defined further down in the same module, but the health
function was using the wrong reference.

Result: every Render health probe failed, which kept the service in a
degraded routing state. The home page was taking 22 seconds to respond
because Render couldn't confirm the instance was healthy. Verified by
curling /api/health and getting 503 + "db.get is not a function".

Fixed by calling the local hoisted get() function directly.

auto-restore decision is made.

- Auto-restore fires when DB_PATH is missing OR < 100 KB (a real DB with

- Suspect file is moved to *.replaced-{ts} aside for forensic review
- Logs the disk probe at boot (DB_PATH exists/size, backupDir exists)

entries.subject: db: fix disk-mount race that wiped DB on every Render deploy
entries.title: db: fix disk-mount race that wiped DB on every Render deploy
entries.body:
ROOT CAUSE of the 2026-05-11 and 2026-05-12 data wipes:
Render's persistent disk mounts asynchronously. The Node process starts
BEFORE /data is fully visible. initDb()'s existsSync(DB_PATH) was
returning FALSE even though the real 24 MB DB file existed on the disk.
That sent boot down the `else` branch (create empty in-memory DB) and
saveDb() at the end of initDb wrote the empty DB over the real file
once /data finished mounting. Silent total data loss every deploy.

FIX (two layers of defense):
1. Retry existsSync for up to 30 seconds (500ms × 60). Wait for /data
   to mount before deciding the file doesn't exist.
2. If main file is still missing AFTER mount confirms (backups dir
   exists), the file genuinely vanished — auto-restore from the
   newest backup in /data/backups/ instead of overwriting with empty.
   Only proceeds with restore if a backup > 100 KB is available (skip
   tiny / corrupted ones).

Either layer alone would have prevented yesterday's wipe; together
they make this class of bug impossible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

entries.subject: Data protection: 5-layer backup + integrity system (never lose data again)
entries.title: Data protection: 5-layer backup + integrity system (never lose data again)
entries.body:
Direct response to today's DB corruption incident. The hub now has
five independent guards against data loss:

LAYER 1 — OFF-RENDER EMAIL BACKUPS (server/backup.js)
  Daily at 2 AM CT, the DB is gzipped and emailed as an attachment to
  BACKUP_RECIPIENTS (defaults to mattsmithremax@gmail.com; comma-separated
  env var). Capped at 25 MB compressed to stay under SendGrid's limit.
  Off-disk copies survive even a total Render outage.

LAYER 2 — PRE-MIGRATION SNAPSHOTS (server/database.js)
  Before any migration runs, initDb() copies the file to
  /data/backups/realestate-hub.db.pre-boot-{ts}. Keeps last 10 boots.
  If a migration corrupts the file, the rollback is one cp away.

LAYER 3 — MIGRATION LEDGER (_migrations table + runMigration helper)
  Each named migration runs at most once. The agency_type CHECK
  recreate-table migration re-ran every boot and slowly corrupted the
  disk for weeks; with the ledger that pattern is impossible. Future
  migrations must use runMigration('descriptive_name', fn).

LAYER 4 — POST-MIGRATION INTEGRITY CHECK
  PRAGMA quick_check on load (was added in 0430e39); PRAGMA
  integrity_check now also runs after migrations. checkDbHealth()
  exported for use by the health endpoint.

LAYER 5 — RENDER HEALTH ENDPOINT (GET /api/health)
  Unauthenticated. Returns 503 if the DB is unqueryable so Render's
  health probe drops the sick instance and keeps the prior healthy
  one routed. Configure the Render service's 'Health Check Path' to
  /api/health to activate.

MANUAL CONTROLS
  POST /api/backup/now      — fire the daily backup right now
  GET  /api/backup/list     — list on-disk backups (for restore UIs)

The disabled agency_type recreate-table migration stays disabled.
Backup file rotation deletes anything older than the last 14 daily +
10 pre-boot copies so the disk doesn't fill up.

entries.subject: db: malformed-file recovery + disable the migration that caused corruption
entries.title: db: malformed-file recovery + disable the migration that caused corruption
entries.body:
Two safety fixes for the production outage caused by a corrupt
realestate-hub.db on Render's persistent disk:

1. initDb() now wraps the load in try/catch + runs PRAGMA quick_check.
   If the file is unreadable ('disk image malformed', etc), it's
   renamed to *.broken-{timestamp} (preserving for later recovery)
   and a fresh empty DB is created so the server can boot. Loud logs

entries.subject: Critical perf fix: Realist import in bulk mode (defers DB save-to-disk)
entries.title: Critical perf fix: Realist import in bulk mode (defers DB save-to-disk)
entries.body:
The hub uses sql.js (SQLite-as-JS-library) which has no separate DB process — every db.run() in the run() helper called saveDb() which writes the ENTIRE DB to disk. With a 50-100MB database and 6,000+ writes during a Realist import, that's 6,000 full DB serializations on the same Node event loop. Result: server completely blocked, clients can't load, browser times out.

Fix:
- New beginBulk()/endBulk() pair on database.js. While in bulk mode, the run() helper skips saveDb() — caller flushes once at the end.
- Realist /import and /rematch now wrap their loops in try { beginBulk(); ... } finally { endBulk() } so disk is hit just twice instead of thousands of times.
- try/finally guarantees the DB is unlocked even on error mid-import.

Expected behavior:
- 3,000-row Realist import: ~5-15 seconds (was 5+ minutes / hung server)
- During import: leads + other endpoints stay responsive between writes (the loop releases the event loop more often)
- After import: one big saveDb() flushes everything to /data/realestate-hub.db

entries.subject: Realist import: O(1) address matching (was 135M LIKE comparisons → now 1 SELECT + map lookup)
entries.title: Realist import: O(1) address matching (was 135M LIKE comparisons → now 1 SELECT + map lookup)
entries.body:
The previous matching loop ran a full table scan with REPLACE/REPLACE/LOWER/LIKE for every property × every client (3000 × 45000 = 135M ops). On Render Starter that took several minutes — long enough that the browser timed out before getting the response, even though properties were actually being inserted.

New approach:
- Load all clients with addresses in one SELECT (45K rows, fast)
- Normalize each address in JS, build Map<normalized_addr, [client_ids]>
- For each property, look up matches with addrMap.get(norm) — O(1)
- Same fix applied to /rematch endpoint

Result: 3000-row Realist CSV import should now finish in 5-15 seconds instead of 5+ minutes. Browser will see the response and show the success alert as expected.

entries.title: transaction date auto-calc: parse as local date (timezone bug) + correct walkthrough rule
entries.body:
The old calc functions called new Date('YYYY-MM-DD') which JS interprets as UTC midnight, then drifted into the previous day in any timezone west of UTC. Result: depending on the user's timezone, calcEarnestDue and calcFinalWalkthrough could produce dates 1 day off (or land on a wrong weekday entirely).

New parseLocalDate() splits the YYYY-MM-DD string and calls the local-time Date constructor — no timezone conversion happens. formatLocalDate() outputs the result back as YYYY-MM-DD using local components. Dates now match the user's intuition exactly.

- Closing Wed 6/10 → Walkthrough Tue 6/9
- Closing Mon 6/8  → Walkthrough Fri 6/5 (skip weekend)
- Closing Sat      → Walkthrough Fri (1 day back)
- Closing Sun      → Walkthrough Fri (skip Sat)
- Earnest Wed 6/10 + 3 biz days → Mon 6/15 (skip Sat/Sun)

entries.subject: Fix Sierra incremental 400: proper UTC ISO date format + show actual API error body
entries.title: Sierra incremental 400: proper UTC ISO date format + show actual API error body
entries.body:
Root cause:
- The 'since' date sent in leadUpdateDateFrom was being mangled: SQLite returns 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' in UTC but without the Z marker, JS Date.parse interprets that as LOCAL time (which on Render UTC servers happens to be right, but on machines with TZ drift it can be hours off and Sierra rejects it as 400)
- The fallback ISO string had milliseconds + Z stripped after .split('.')[0] — leaving a bare 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' with no timezone, which Sierra appears to reject

Fixes:
- New toSierraDate() helper normalizes any input (Date, ISO string, SQLite datetime string) to clean ISO 8601 UTC with Z marker (e.g. '2026-05-04T19:30:00Z')
- Cap 'since' window to a max of 7 days back (no point pulling older incrementally; also defensively prevents very-old-date rejection)
- Filter sync_log lookups to skip error rows when computing 'last successful sync'
- Falls back through last successful incremental → last successful full sync → 7 days ago

entries.title: Listings save: show errors, close modal on success, jump to new stage tab
entries.body:
The save function silently swallowed errors and never closed the modal — so when changing Stage to Under Contract (or any other field), it looked like nothing was happening:
- The PUT was actually succeeding
- The modal stayed open showing the same form, so user thought save failed
- Meanwhile the card in the background moved to the new stage's column, but the user couldn't see it because they were on a different stage tab

Fixes:
- Wrap save in try/catch — alerts the user if save fails
- Close modal on successful save (matches Transactions UX)
- If stage changed and user was filtering by a specific stage, auto-switch the filter to the new stage so the card is visible right away
